decisions.action: Maintain wrapper APIs and enforce parity checks.

decisions.rationale: Native Gaussian NLL kernel is strong; wrappers provide ergonomic mask/weight support and log-variance handling.
decisions.action: Keep wrappers and lock numerical agreement against native behavior.

known_divergences: wrapper accepts both variance and log-variance conventions while native API expects variance

decisions.rationale: Needed for regression-as-classification workflows with consistent masking/weighting semantics.
decisions.action: Retain wrappers and parity tests, document intended scope.

decisions.rationale: Avoid reinvention; align baseline metric behavior with community-standard implementations.
decisions.action: Prefer thin wrappers and parity checks against torchmetrics.

known_divergences: sample_weight and non-mean reductions remain torchregress-specific wrapper semantics

decisions.rationale: Regression calibration/PIT metrics require task-specific semantics not fully covered by native classification-focused primitives.
decisions.action: Keep custom implementations with explicit contracts and targeted tests.

decisions.rationale: Composite OOD reporting is task-specific, but core discrimination primitives should remain native-backed.

decisions.action: Retain custom API while relying on vectorized native tensor ops internally.

decisions.rationale: No direct native equivalent exists for regression conformal workflows and interval-generation policy.
decisions.action: Keep custom conformal stack and maintain coverage/width governance tests.

decisions.rationale: EIV formulations are specialized and not covered by native torch loss modules.
decisions.action: Keep custom implementations with targeted stability and comparison coverage.

decisions.rationale: These utilities should remain compatibility wrappers around native performance primitives.
decisions.action: Keep wrappers minimal and behavior-aligned with upstream.

known_divergences: wrapper includes graceful fallback paths for unsupported devices/runtime failures

decisions.rationale: torchmetrics SSIM is image-only (4-D/5-D, no mask or weights, batch-global data range); a [B, 1, N, 1] reshape with a (k, 1) kernel reproduces its score but cannot express masked/weighted local moments, coverage-based window exclusion, per-row data range, valid-only windows or arbitrary leading dims. The custom path is one native conv1d over stacked moment channels.
decisions.action: Keep the conv1d implementation and lock parity with torchmetrics on [B, 1, N, 1] inputs (reflect padding: score; valid padding: cropped map) and with a direct per-window NumPy reference for masks and weights.

known_divergences: default padding='valid' scores only windows fully inside the sequence; torchmetrics 1.9 averages reflect-padded windows (padding='reflect' matches it)
default data_range is the per-row target range; torchmetrics uses max(range(preds), range(target)) over the whole batch
moments are formed after a per-row shift, so the map differs from torchmetrics' uncentred E[x^2] - E[x]^2 at round-off level

decisions.rationale: LowRankMultivariateNormal has the same covariance structure but needs the factor materialised per row, has no per-sample masks, no flat (improper) priors and no nuisance posterior; MarginalizedMultiSourceGaussianNLLLoss gives the same NLL for diagonal known noise but materialises a dense [B, N, N] measurement covariance and a per-row Jacobian (about 819 GB at B=1024, N=10k in float64), has no flat priors and no posterior, and copies a shared basis per row; the custom path uses native batched matmul, cholesky_ex and cholesky_solve on m x m systems.
decisions.action: Keep the Woodbury implementation and lock equality with MultivariateNormal and LowRankMultivariateNormal for proper priors.

known_divergences: flat prior directions return the improper p(a)=1 marginal, i.e. the restricted likelihood (REML) with its constants (tested against error contrasts); torch.distributions has no improper priors
rows whose posterior precision is not numerically positive definite raise instead of returning a jittered value

decisions.rationale: torch.distributions has no multivariate Student-t, no masked (marginal) log densities, no linear-observation or censored likelihoods, no conditioning and no mixture quantiles; StudentTMixture subclasses torch.distributions.Distribution and uses native batched cholesky_ex, solve_triangular, cholesky_solve, QR, Categorical and Chi2, with the components folded into the batch.
decisions.action: Keep the custom distribution; lock parity with scipy multivariate_t / multivariate_normal / t and torch MultivariateNormal.

known_divergences: noisy linear observations and conditioning treat the Gaussian noise as sharing the t mixing variable (exact for df = inf); the exact density of A x + e with independent Gaussian e is not a Student-t
MixtureDensityLoss no longer adds eps to the diagonal scales inside the log density (scales are floored by min_std); Gaussian NLLs differ from the previous release by O(eps / min_std)

decisions.rationale: MultivariateNormal evaluates the same density once the caller assembles C_known + diag(s^2) + U U^T, but has no per-dimension masks (exact marginals), no equilibration (scipy rejects, and float32 loses accuracy on, badly scaled covariances), no learned fractional scatter, no reported jitter and no chi2 / whitened-residual outputs; the custom path pads masked dimensions to blockdiag(C_oo, I) and calls native batched cholesky_ex and solve_triangular on the equilibrated matrix.
decisions.action: Keep the thin custom wrapper over native batched Cholesky; lock parity with scipy, MultivariateGaussianLoss, LowRankGaussianLoss and the Woodbury path of marginalize_linear_nuisance.

known_divergences: about 1.6x the cost of a bare MultivariateNormal on a caller-assembled covariance (padding, equilibration and validation passes over [B, D, D])
rows whose equilibrated covariance is not numerically positive definite raise unless max_jitter > 0; the jitter is relative to the diagonal and reported per row
